A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TagSpeech and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Retained content can be matched across section and table renumbering, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original AMI and AliMeeting benchmark results, encoder and temporal-anchor ablations, and error analyses in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds regional overlap analysis, zero-shot cross-language evaluation, and results under an additional DER collar.

M1.justification: The dual encoders, SOT fine-tuning, numeric time anchors, XML-style input/output, frozen LLM, and projector-only training remain unchanged. LoRA adaptation is proposed only as future work.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates separately trained models within AMI and AliMeeting. v2 additionally tests AMI-trained models on AliMeeting and vice versa without adaptation, adding cross-language and acoustic-shift scenarios while retaining the same corpora, languages, and underlying task.

E2.justification: Existing comparisons retain Gemini-2.0-flash, both Qwen-Omni models, Pyannote plus Whisper, and the encoder and temporal-cue controls. Qwen naming changes identify the same models. The new regional analysis reuses the cascade baseline and SOT controls without establishing a new comparison method.

E3.justification: v2 adds zero-shot cross-corpus testing, reference-derived UEM masks for separate overlap/non-overlap scoring, and DER evaluation with a 0.25-second collar alongside the retained zero-collar evaluation. Existing dataset splits, training settings, and primary evaluation protocol remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Section 5.2 and Table 5 directly examine overlap handling using regional DER and models with and without SOT. Section 4.4 and Appendix A.4 add cross-language robustness tests exposing transcription collapse, while Appendix A.5 checks collar sensitivity. These substantially extend the questions investigated beyond the retained encoder/anchor ablations and case studies.

E5.justification: The single-run, fixed-random-seed statement is retained from v1 Appendix A.4 in v2 Appendix A.5. No repeated-run estimates, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: Existing main and ablation scores are retained, but substantial new findings are reported. Table 5 gives AliMeeting overlap DER of 33.68% for TagSpeech versus 53.11% for the cascade. Table 8 reports cross-language DER of 19.99%/26.53%, failure rates of 28.20%/22.94%, and cpWER above 100% in both directions. Tables 9–10 add 0.25-second-collar results, including TagSpeech DER of 18.73% on AMI and 16.18% on AliMeeting.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, projector and anchor equations, structured input, autoregressive objective, and appendix metric formulas are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and principal conclusion retain the same claims about explicit transcription/speaker/timestamp prediction, lightweight temporal grounding, parameter-efficient training, and DER advantages over end-to-end baselines. The added experiments do not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: v2 introduces an interpretation separating language-independent temporal grounding from language-dependent transcription, attributing transfer failure to training-language hallucination and LLM bias. Section 5.2 adds an explanation of the cascade's non-overlap advantage through boundary precision versus TagSpeech's overlap advantage. Section 4.3 also corrects the cascade comparison: TagSpeech trails it on AMI but surpasses it on AliMeeting.

D1.justification: The first-page availability statement now includes the model alongside code and demo. Table 2 explicitly states that metrics other than failure rate use successful outputs. Appendix A.2 retains the same implementation, hyperparameter, hardware, and training-time details.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive research positioning are retained. Revised Section 2.1 repeats the distinction between timestamped diarization and speaker-attributed transcription already present in v1's introduction. Completing the Lhotse authorship is a bibliographic correction, not a new cited work.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose, grammar, and model-name edits, adds subsections for the new analyses, and renumbers retained sections. Section 5.1 is retitled, and acknowledgements are expanded. The overall narrative structure and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 5, 8, and 10 and expands the former Table 7, now Table 9, to display paired zero- and 0.25-second-collar DER values. Table 2 gains an explanatory footnote. All five figures are retained, with limited caption and placement changes within the existing layout.

improvement.justification: v2 improves evidential clarity through direct overlap comparisons, alternate-collar checks, and disclosure of previously untested cross-language transcription failure. It also corrects the discussion of the cascade baseline. These are useful gains, but the language-independent grounding interpretation remains stronger than the evidence establishes: cross-language DER excludes failed outputs despite failure rates of 22.94–28.20%.
